NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's web site under City Council Meeting agendas at www.RollingHillsEstates.gov and
  during regular business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's web
  site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP -TV
  Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to
  address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public comment, please
  complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 8, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by members MAYOR SCHMITZ.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Stegura

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Steve McEwen
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING  OCTOBER  2024  "BREAST  CANCER
  AWARENESS MONTH"

MAYOR SCHMITZ presented a proclamation declaring October 2024 as “Breast Cancer
Awareness Month.” Assistant City Manager Davis accepted the Proclamation on behalf of
Evelyn Calip, Nurse Navigator at the Vasek and Anna Maria Polak Breast Diagnostic Center
at Torrance Memorial Medical Center.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-F AS FOLLOWS
  BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF SEPTEMBER & OCTOBER 2024

  APPROVED WARRANTS 67842 THROUGH 67867 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $112,536.84, AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090424 THROUGH
  090524; IN THE AMOUNT OF $90,723.68; FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $203,260.50 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 24, 2024

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 8, 2024
 D.  R PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 17, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  RESOLUTION NO. 2587 CONTINUING THE PROCLAMATION OF THE LOCAL
  EMERGENCY ARISING FROM SIGNIFICANT LAND MOVEMENT ALONG AND IN
  THE VICINITY OF PEARTREE LANE IN THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION NO. 2587 CONTINUING THE PROCLAMATION
  OF A LOCAL EMERGENCY CAUSED BY SIGNIFICANT LAND MOVEMENT
  ON PEARTREE LANE.

F.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS BOARD MEETING
  HIGHLIGHTS OF AUGUST 22, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON RELIABILITY REPORT

Constance Turner, Government Relations Manager for Southern California Edison, provided a
presentation on SCE’s reliability report, including strengthening and modernizing the grid,
reducing wildfire risk, 2023 year-end progress update and public safety power shutoffs.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING.

**ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING**

A.  2024 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE DEBRIEF AND 2025 DATE CHANGE

  Recommendation: That the Pepper Tree Foundation Executive Board receive and file
  the debrief report and consider changing the date of the Hills Are Alive Race from the
  first Saturday of August to Saturday, May 31, 2025.

Community Services Coordinator Morrow provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

MEMBER HUFF agreed that the weather will be cooler in May than it is in August and
confirmed with staff that the Hermosa Beach race does not conflict with this date change.

MEMBER ZERUNYAN and CHAIR SCHMITZ discussed student participation, which would
hopefully increase with the new date earlier in the year.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MEMBER ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS
  FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE DEBRIEF REPORT AND DIRECT STAFF TO
  CHANGE THE DATE OF THE HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE FROM THE FIRST
  SATURDAY OF AUGUST TO SATURDAY, MAY 31, 2025.

CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 8, 2024
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING.

**RECONVENE TO CITY COUNCIL MEETING**

B.  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT AND PROPOSAL FOR PROFESSIONAL
  GIS SERVICES FOR THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Authorize the City Manager to enter into
  the Professional Services Agreement with Infinity Technologies to provide GIS
  services to the Community Development Department, in a not-to-exceed amount of
  $21,500 for Year 1, to the satisfaction of the City Attorney; and 2) Approve a budget
  adjustment in Account No. 4220-439 adding $7,500, for a new total account budget
  of $72,500.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO ENTER INTO THE PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH INFINITY TECHNOLOGIES TO PROVIDE
  GIS SERVICES TO THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT, IN A
  NOT-TO-EXCEED AMOUNT OF $21,500 FOR YEAR 1, TO THE
  SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY; AND 2) APPROVE A BUDGET
  ADJUSTMENT IN ACCOUNT NO. 4220-439 ADDING $7,500, FOR A NEW
  TOTAL ACCOUNT BUDGET OF $72,500.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

C.  COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE LOCAL APPOINTMENT  LIST  AND
  APPOINTMENT PROCESS FOR EXPIRING TERMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the Commission/Committee
  appointment process for expiring terms and receive and file this report.

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

D.  THIRD AMENDMENT TO CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Third Amendment to City
  Manager Employment Agreement and authorize its execution by the Mayor.

Assistant City Attorney McEwen provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked the City Manager and staff for their loyalty,
especially when there have been years when no salary increases could be provided.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 8, 2024
 MAYOR SCHMITZ echoed COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s comments, and thanked
City Manager Grammer for his dedication, leadership and for the culture he has created
within the City.

City Manager Grammer thanked the City Council for their support.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE THE THIRD AMENDMENT TO CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT
  AGREEMENT AND AUTHORIZE ITS EXECUTION BY THE MAYOR.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF announced the Cal Cities Annual Conference will be held in
Long Beach next week, as well as the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce’s
Legislative Luncheon next Friday, October 18.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN announced the CJPIA Annual Risk Management
Educational Forum being held this week, with Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
nominated for a second year in a row for the Capstone Award.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN also announced the California Contract Cities
Association’s (CCCA) City Managers Summit at USC on October 24.

MAYOR SCHMITZ and COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN attended the Rollingwood HOA’s
annual meeting earlier this evening and discussed the state of the City.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

None.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS Government Code Section 54957.6
  Agency Designated Representatives: City Manager and Assistant City Manager
  Employee Organization: City of Rolling Hills Estates Employees' Association

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:52 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned to Tuesday, October 22, 2024 at 7:00 p.m. for
the purpose of a Regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Velveth Schmitz, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 8, 2024
